subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The symbol ⇌ in an equation shows that the reaction is:
questions.explain: The ⇌ symbol indicates a reversible reaction.

questions.q: A reaction is exothermic overall when:
options: More energy is released making bonds than absorbed breaking bonds
Equal energy is absorbed and released
More energy is absorbed breaking bonds than released making bonds
questions.explain: If bond-making releases more energy than bond-breaking absorbs, the reaction is exothermic overall.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system:
options: The forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate
All reactants have been used up
questions.explain: At equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.q: A solution has a pH of 12. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: A pH greater than 7 indicates an alkaline (basic) solution.

questions.q: Why is a catalyst often used in industry even though it does not increase yield?
options: It is used up so must be replaced
It gives a useful rate at lower temperatures, saving energy
questions.explain: Catalysts allow a fast enough rate at lower temperatures, reducing energy costs.

questions.q: Hydrochloric acid is described as a strong acid because it:
questions.explain: A strong acid such as HCl ionises fully in water, releasing all its H+ ions.

questions.q: If the concentration of a reactant is increased in a system at equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts to:
questions.explain: Adding more reactant shifts the equilibrium towards the products to oppose the change.

questions.q: Is bond making endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Forming new bonds releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: Powdered marble reacts faster with acid than a single marble chip of the same mass because:
options: The powder has a larger surface area
questions.explain: Breaking the solid into powder exposes a larger surface area, so collisions are more frequent.

questions.q: Which graph result shows that a reaction has finished?
options: The line falls back to zero
questions.explain: When no more product forms the line levels off (becomes horizontal), showing the reaction is complete.

questions.q: On the reaction profile of an exothermic reaction, the products are:
options: At the same energy as the reactants
Higher in energy than the reactants
Lower in energy than the reactants
questions.explain: In an exothermic reaction the products have less energy than the reactants, so the line ends lower.

questions.q: In a simple chemical cell, a greater voltage is produced when the two metals are:
options: Further apart in the reactivity series
questions.explain: The bigger the difference in reactivity between the two metals, the larger the voltage produced.

questions.q: When making a soluble salt from an insoluble base and acid, why is excess base added?
options: To ensure all the acid is neutralised
questions.explain: Excess insoluble base guarantees all the acid reacts; the leftover solid is then filtered off.

questions.q: The overall energy change of a reaction can be calculated as:
options: Energy to break bonds minus energy to make bonds
Energy to make bonds minus energy to break bonds
questions.explain: Energy change = energy in to break bonds minus energy out from making bonds.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of a reaction?
options: Increasing the surface area of a solid reactant
questions.explain: A larger surface area gives more sites for collisions, increasing the rate.

questions.q: Adding a catalyst changes a reaction profile by:
options: Raising the energy of the products
Lowering the energy of the reactants
questions.explain: A catalyst provides a route with a lower activation energy, shown as a smaller hump on the profile.

questions.q: Which everyday substance is alkaline?
questions.explain: Soap solution has a pH above 7, making it alkaline, while the others are acidic.

questions.q: Two acids have the same concentration but acid X has a lower pH than acid Y. What can you conclude?
options: Acid Y is a stronger acid
Acid X is a stronger acid
questions.explain: At equal concentration, the acid that ionises more (lower pH) is the stronger acid.

questions.q: Increasing the pressure on a gaseous equilibrium shifts it towards:
options: The side with more gas molecules
The side with fewer gas molecules
questions.explain: Le Chatelier: higher pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce pressure.

questions.q: Which process is endothermic and is used in instant cold packs?
options: Dissolving certain salts such as ammonium nitrate
questions.explain: Dissolving ammonium nitrate takes in energy from the surroundings, cooling the pack.

questions.q: In a hydrogen fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen combine to produce:
questions.explain: A hydrogen fuel cell produces only water (and electrical energy) as hydrogen reacts with oxygen.

questions.q: Which name correctly describes ethanoic acid?
questions.explain: Ethanoic acid only partially ionises in water, so it is a weak acid.
